messages:
harper: hey folks, day 3 here. quick: i'm toggling between hosted and sandbox keys for local dev. i ran a streaming sample and saw several 429s after a few seconds. is hosted allowed for local sandboxing or should i stick to sandbox keys?

lee: welcome! stick to sandbox for casual local dev. hosted keys are for staging/prod and have different quota buckets and billing. sandbox streaming quotas are intentionally lower to keep dev noise down.

harper: thanks. i actually can't find the sandbox key in Console -> API Keys. only a hosted key shows up in my profile.

ravi: if the sandbox entry is missing it could mean your org's sandbox credits were exhausted or provisioning didn't finish. open Console -> API Keys -> Org dropdown -> check the "Sandbox" tab. If absent, file a provisioning request via the internal form and cc #eng-infra.

harper: got it. FYI the 429 payload included: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","rate_bucket":"sb-stream-alpha","retry_after":2}. is that the expected format?

devops-bot: Yes. Please include full response when filing. For streaming, rate_bucket values like sb-stream-alpha or sb-stream-small indicate dev buckets. Quota increase URL: https://intranet.redwood/company-forms/compute-quota

lee: also avoid aggressive retry loops in local tests. use exponential backoff, honor Retry-After, and throttle message rate while iterating on prompts. For demos that need steady streaming, request a temporary dev bump and note "new hire demo".

onboarding-bot: Welcome, harper! :wave: Helpful links: Getting started with Sandbox keys - https://intranet.redwood/docs/dev-keys • Streaming best practices - https://intranet.redwood/docs/streaming-guide.

harper: sweet, thanks. i'll check Console, submit the quota form if needed, and paste the raw 429 if it persists. appreciate the tips :thumbsup:
